candidates.failure_reason: U113 Part III: the Chabauty-Coleman route bounds the WRONG OBJECT. U99 proves rank_Z J^-(k) <= 2 < g = 8 over k = Q(sqrt5), giving #C^-(k) <= 9. But U105 own "degree obstruction" shows a positive integer solution yields c = i*2^(4/5), whose minimal polynomial is x^10 + 256 (verified exactly), of degree 10 over k. Solutions therefore give points of C^-(L) with [L:k] = 10, which are not elements of C^-(k). A bound on the k-rational points is silent about them, so "C^-(k) contains no points from solutions, therefore no solutions" is a non sequitur with a vacuously true premise. Closing this needs Chabauty over L (degree 20 over Q) with rank_Z J^-(L) < 8 RE-ESTABLISHED (ranks grow in extensions), or symmetric-power Chabauty / covering collections. None exists in U99, U102 or U105.

candidates.claim: RESTART on the single converged obstruction (no Frey-type object for three INDEPENDENT exponents), and an EXACT reason the rigid-local-system route cannot supply one. Katz rigidity index on P^1 minus {0,1,inf} for rank n is rig = -n^2 + sum over the three punctures of the sum of squares of the local eigenvalue multiplicities, and the system is rigid iff rig = 2. If all three local monodromies are REGULAR SEMISIMPLE — which is exactly the case of monodromy of orders x,y,z acting with distinct eigenvalues — then rig = -n^2+3n = 2, forcing n = 1 or n = 2 and nothing else.

The classical Frey curve does NOT carry the exponents as monodromy orders: it carries them through the valuation of its discriminant, and level lowering then removes them entirely. PSS used a nonabelian descent to twists of the Klein quartic (genus 3), and Siksek-Stoll and Dahmen-Siksek used descent plus Chabauty. The obstruction remains real for the route the survey names as live, but it is not a barrier to the classical method — which is exactly why the classical method still closes signatures, one at a time.

candidates.claim: THE OBSTRUCTION IN THE OTHER PICTURE — the discriminant-valuation Frey curve that C130 showed the rigidity bounds do NOT cover. (a) For the STANDARD two-term Frey curve E: Y^2 = X(X-a)(X+b) with a=A^x, b=B^y, c=C^z, the discriminant is 16(abc)^2, and Ribet level lowering strips a bad prime l exactly when p divides v_l(Delta). candidates.claim: C171 UNDERSTATED THE OBSTRUCTION. The three-exponent rigid Q-rational object is never REGULAR. Regularity (distinct Hodge-Tate weights, required by every potential-automorphy theorem available in rank > 2) means partition (1^n) at both 0 and infinity; those contribute n+n, so rig = 2 forces the third puncture to contribute n^2-2n+2, i.e. the pseudoreflection (n-1,1); and a pseudoreflection is Q-rational only when phi(m) = 1, i.e. m <= 2, excluded by the Beal exponent range. So automorphy is not merely unproved for this object -- the regular-weight family of theorems cannot apply to it however much it is strengthened.
candidates.method: Exhaustive exact enumeration, code/U317_regularity_obstruction.py: of 792 rigid Q-rational triples with three pairwise distinct reduced exponents at ranks 2..14, ZERO are regular at both 0 and infinity; and (n-1,1) is Q-rational for NO reduced exponent at any rank 3..8. Self-duality was checked too and is free: a Galois orbit over Q is closed under alpha -> alpha^(-1) because -1 is coprime to m, so only regularity bites.
candidates.evidence: Arithmetic core machine-checked in formal/Beal/Rigidity.lean: regular_forces_pseudoreflection (rigidityIndex n (n+n+s) = 2 iff s = n^2-2n+2), pseudoreflection_budget, rational_pseudoreflection_order_le_two (via Nat.totient_eq_one_iff), no_rational_pseudoreflection_for_exponent. #print axioms = [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]; full lake build clean.

evaluations.estimate_corrected_U343: MY OWN ESTIMATE WAS TOO LOW, corrected. C177 said EulerDescentStep needs 'a few hundred lines' because mathlib has three_pid (IsPrincipalIdealRing for the ring of integers of Q(zeta_3)). That is necessary but NOT sufficient, and the missing piece is the classical trap in this exact descent. The norm form of Z[omega] is a^2 - ab + b^2, not a^2 + 3b^2. Exact identity, verified over |p|,|q| <= 25 with zero mismatches: p + q*sqrt(-3) = (p+q) + 2q*omega, so p^2 + 3q^2 = N_omega(p+q, 2q) -- whose SECOND coordinate is always EVEN. Z[sqrt(-3)] sits inside Z[omega] with index 2, and a factorisation valid in Z[omega] does not descend without a parity argument. Witness: N_omega(1,1) = 1, but (1,1) is not of the form ((p+q), 2q) for any integers p,q. So the formalisation needs the index-2 bookkeeping on top of the UFD property, and 'a few hundred lines' should be read as a LOWER BOUND. This is also exactly why the naive Euler descent in Z[sqrt(-3)] is unsound -- the historical flaw in Euler's own argument, which PSS mention in passing ('Euler's argument had a flaw, but it was later fixed by others').
